newsitem.title: UK: IBCA gives Taiwan's Hua Nan Bank individual rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA gives Taiwan's Hua Nan Bank individual rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it assigned Hua Nan Commerical Bank of Taiwan an individual rating of B/C.
Its legal rating of 2 remains unchanged.
Hua Nan is one of the three large, majority government owned commerical banks operating in Taiwan, where it commands a six percent share of the loan and deposit markets.
"Hua Nan's performance and capitalisation are fair, with the bank maintaining a slight edge over its peers in terms of its financial profile," IBCA said in a statement.
As with most banks in Taiwan, it is experiencing a decline in its asset quality, but from a high level by relative standards, IBCA said.

Market share has also fallen as a result of competition from the newly established private banks, but its majority government shareholding and extensive branch network should ensure that its deposit base remains stable, IBCA said.

IBCA's individual rating is an evaluation of the bank's financial strength based on the premise that it is entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners.
The highest individual rating awarded by IBCA is A. Legal ratings are evaluated on the basis of the likelihood of support from owners or government authorities if it ran into difficulties.
